<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914734_theRebbe_896" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914734_theRebbe_896__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the return of the soul to G-d is primarily achieved through the service of teshuvah, which transcends the measured service of the righteous.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, this matter of "and the spirit shall return to G-d who gave it"</t>
    <t s="2">[that even when the soul is below, it will be unified with Him, blessed be He, just as it was included in the Essence of Ein Sof]</t>
    <t s="3">is primarily through the service of teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="4">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="5">that this is also hinted at in the language of the verse "and the spirit shall return,"</t>
    <t s="6">"shall return" from the term teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="7">for the essence of the return of the soul to its root</t>
    <t s="8">(to G-d who gave it)</t>
    <t s="9">is through the service of teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="10">And the explanation is</t>
    <t s="11">(as explained in the maamar),</t>
    <t s="12">that the service of the righteous</t>
    <t s="13">(Torah, service [prayer], and acts of kindness)</t>
    <t s="14">is within measure and limitation,</t>
    <t s="15">whereas the service of teshuvah is beyond measure and limitation.</t>
    <t s="16">For this is that teshuvah is in one hour and in one moment.</t>
    <t s="17">Therefore, the return of the soul to its root through teshuvah is a return more elevated than the return through Torah, service, and acts of kindness</t>
    <t s="18">(the service of the righteous).</t>
    <t s="19">And this is "Peace, peace, to the far and to the near,"</t>
    <t s="20">to the far first and then to the near,</t>
    <t s="21">that the peace made through the service of teshuvah</t>
    <t s="22">(the far who has been brought near)</t>
    <t s="23">is more elevated than the peace through the service of the righteous</t>
    <t s="24">(the near).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section compares teshuvah to a healing that requires only a single drop, because it stems from a power beyond limitation, which is why the verse says "G-d said, and I will heal him."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is also what the verse continues, "G-d said, and I will heal him,"</t>
    <t s="1">for the advantage of the service of teshuvah</t>
    <t s="2">(peace to the far)</t>
    <t s="3">is that teshuvah is like a healing</t>
    <t s="4">("and I will heal him").</t>
    <t s="5">And the explanation is</t>
    <t s="6">(as explained in the maamar),</t>
    <t s="7">that with eating and drinking, a large quantity of food is needed to effect a strengthening of the soul's connection to the limbs of the body,</t>
    <t s="8">but not so with healing,</t>
    <t s="9">even one drop of medicinal spices has the power to strengthen the soul's connection to the body.</t>
    <t s="10">And the reason for this is,</t>
    <t s="11">that the power in medicinal spices is not as limited as the power in food,</t>
    <t s="12">and therefore it is not so dependent on quantity.</t>
    <t s="13">And analogously, this is so with teshuvah, which is compared to a healing,</t>
    <t s="14">that the reason for this, that teshuvah is in one hour and in one moment,</t>
    <t s="15">and even that through one thought of teshuvah one is transformed from a complete wicked person to a complete righteous person,</t>
    <t s="16">is,</t>
    <t s="17">because teshuvah is beyond limitation.</t>
    <t s="18">Based on this, we can explain what is written, "G-d said, and I will heal him,"</t>
    <t s="19">that regarding healing and teshuvah it says "G-d said"</t>
    <t s="20">(even though the action of all things is not through their own power but through the power of the Holy One, blessed be He),</t>
    <t s="21">it is,</t>
    <t s="22">because in healing and in teshuvah there is a matter that is beyond limitation</t>
    <t s="23">[therefore,</t>
    <t s="24">teshuvah is in one hour and in one moment,</t>
    <t s="25">and analogously, literal healing can also be through a single drop],</t>
    <t s="26">and this matter is through a bestowal of special power from Above,</t>
    <t s="27">"G-d said."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the healing of "I am G-d your healer" comes from G-d Himself, erasing any trace of the malady retroactively.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And we may add</t>
    <t s="2">[and particularly since this matter</t>
    <t s="3">(below)</t>
    <t s="4">is something that the generation needs and many need it],</t>
    <t s="5">that the explanation of "and I will heal him" is that I</t>
    <t s="6">(G-d)</t>
    <t s="7">will heal.</t>
    <t s="8">That is,</t>
    <t s="9">that in addition to the fact that healing in general</t>
    <t s="10">(even when the healing is through an agent,</t>
    <t s="11">a human being)</t>
    <t s="12">is through "G-d said,"</t>
    <t s="13">this healing is drawn from the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself,</t>
    <t s="14">"I am G-d your healer."</t>
    <t s="15">And therefore it is in a manner of "all the illness... I will not place upon you"</t>
    <t s="16">(from the outset).</t>
    <t s="17">And to add,</t>
    <t s="18">that even when the healing of "I am G-d your healer" comes after, due to various causes, an undesirable thing occurred,</t>
    <t s="19">the healing is in a manner that no trace remains,</t>
    <t s="20">and even to the point that it is uprooted retroactively.</t>
    <t s="21">For healing through a human being,</t>
    <t s="22">in addition to the fact that it only heals from now onward,</t>
    <t s="23">even afterwards a trace remains.</t>
    <t s="24">But through the healing of "I am G-d your healer," it is uprooted from its very beginning.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
